symbols.note: copied from `gatekit symbols system <name> --dll dx11 --full` (addresses are bg3_dx11.exe; the Toolkit's own methods without an address were not found in the game binary and are listed with address null; the per-frame update address is not printed for bg3_dx11.exe by this command, it was found by reading the factory in pseudo-code). Parsed by script from the command output, not retyped.
symbols.limits: reads/writes: the component views in the parameters of the system's exported methods. uses: the component operations (add, remove, get, has) its per-frame update performs through the engine's out-of-line helpers, itself or in a function it calls (depth 2), with the call site; kind index: a matched method reads the type's index and the operation is not known. Not listed: operations the compiler inlined, those deeper than depth 2, and what a method that is not the update does (e.g. a SystemLoad) - read its pseudo-code; an empty writes list is not "writes nothing".

does.text: Recomputes threat ranges and writes eoc::combat::ThreatRangeComponent, which is three floats. Several modified-kind query loops (seven query walks in the update) gather entities; for each, a spell id is built and looked up through a manager the system holds, and a range of three floats is worked out. If the entity had no ThreatRangeComponent one is created with those floats; if it had one, each float that differs is updated and a helper raises ThreatRangeChangedEventOneFrameComponent. Entities for which the computation does not complete are listed, and the component is removed from listed entities at the end.
does.evidence: bg3_dx11.exe factory 0x234CBF0 -> entry 0x238F470 -> update 0x3242F30 (1295 lines); create path allocates 12 bytes for ThreatRangeComponent; event helper 0x3245D60 allocates ThreatRangeChangedEventOneFrame; final loop removes ThreatRangeComponent. Read as pseudo-code.
